transcript.text: Alright everyone, we've got a stability sprint coming up — ten business days, capacity for one primary technical-debt focus. The backlog has three candidates: legacy_csv_exporter, webhook_retry_service, and admin_search_index. Before I lock the plan, I want to do our normal round-robin check-in. Let's start with backend engineering — what's your perspective on these three candidates and which one you think should be the priority?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While finishing an unrelated export ticket this afternoon, I confirmed that legacy_csv_exporter already has six of its eight endpoint migrations completed. Exactly two endpoints remain, and the backend team can finish those two within this sprint. I haven't updated the planning board yet.

transcript.text: I need to flag something urgent before we go further. Minutes ago I confirmed in the dependency scanner that legacy_csv_exporter still packages libxml 3.9.4, which has a known exploitable parsing vulnerability. The approved remediation target is exactly libxml 4.1.0. I was verifying scanner results and haven't filed the security finding yet, but given Devon just indicated this work is nearly complete and could be finished this sprint, I strongly recommend legacy_csv_exporter be the sprint focus so we can remediate this vulnerability.
